question: Should explicit requester adoption of descendant output count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester’s later outward send fails?
rationale: The patch deliberately suppresses descendant retry and finalization after requester consumption; tests can verify implementation, but they cannot choose this product delivery boundary.

options.title: Accept consumption with proof
options.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as delivery, contingent on live persisted-state proof for consumed and unconsumed descendants.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Preserve descendant retry until the requester result is successfully sent outward.

options.title: Use durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve the case through the broader completion inbox or spool contract.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption with proof
recommendation.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as delivery, contingent on live persisted-state proof for consumed and unconsumed descendants.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available recent-main routing signal spans the cron fallback and persisted registry surfaces where this boundary is enforced.
